clause_evidence.reasoning: All 21 samples require learners to actively engage with presenting data through pictographic representation, whether by creating pictographs from numerical data or reading pictographs to fill tables. The action of presentation is central to every task.

Ten samples present raw numerical data (item counts organized by category) that learners must convert into pictographs using specified scales. These create-or-complete tasks demonstrate handling of raw data as a source for pictographic representation.

All 21 samples involve numerical data handling in either direction of transformation. Every problem requires learners to work with counts, scales, and conversions, demonstrating comprehensive engagement with data as the centerpiece of pictographic work.

Eleven samples use FillInTable visual format and explicitly ask learners to record data in table structures with category and count columns. These tasks demonstrate learners engaging with data representation in tabular form as specified.

All 21 samples center pictographs as the core representation form. Every problem uses emoji-based symbols (apples, palettes, paw prints, stars, books, basketballs) to represent scaled data. Learners either create pictographs or read them to extract values, establishing pictographs as the essential mathematical representation.

All 21 samples explicitly define and require application of a scale value. Three scale options (2, 5, 10) appear across the collection. Every problem stem and hint references the specific scale multiplier, ensuring learners consistently practice scale interpretation in both reading and creation tasks.

Sample collection demonstrates bidirectional competency across both conversion directions. Ten samples require converting raw data to pictographs; eleven samples require converting pictographs to tabular data. This balanced coverage establishes that learners work with data transformation in both directions as specified by the competency statement.
